senses.definition: A pocket inside the cheek of some animals for carrying food.
senses.example: An eastern chipmunk stuffed its cheek pouch with seeds.

senses.definition: Food saved in a hidden place for later.
senses.example: The chickadee returned to its food cache in the bark.

senses.definition: A long period when an animal’s body slows down to use less energy, often during winter.
senses.example: The groundhog went into hibernation beneath the ground.

senses.definition: A kind of mammal with young that are born at a very early stage and keep growing while they nurse. Many young marsupials develop inside a pouch on their mother.
senses.example: An opossum is a marsupial that carries its tiny babies in a pouch.

senses.definition: The hard part that sticks out from a bird’s mouth. It can also be called a beak.
senses.example: The cardinal held a seed in its bird bill.

senses.definition: A sweet liquid made by many flowers that some animals drink for food.
senses.example: The hummingbird used its tongue to drink nectar.

senses.definition: A box built to give an animal a sheltered place to raise its young.
senses.example: A female wood duck used the nest box set near the pond.

senses.definition: Reaching into shallow water to feed without diving fully under it.
senses.example: The mallard’s tail pointed upward while it was dabbling.

senses.definition: A place where a bird or some other animals rest or sleep.
senses.example: At dusk the turkey flew up to its roost.

senses.definition: Resting in the sun or another warm place to gain heat.
senses.example: The painted turtles were basking on a sunny log.

senses.definition: A pouch under the throat of some animals, including many frogs, that can fill with air and help them make loud calls.
senses.example: The spring peeper’s vocal sac puffed up as it called.

senses.definition: The young swimming stage of a frog or toad, before it loses its long tail and takes its adult shape.
senses.example: A tadpole swam between two stems near the pond edge.

senses.definition: The young stage of some insects that lives in water before becoming an adult.
senses.example: The dragonfly spent its early months as an aquatic nymph.

senses.definition: The release of pollen when a bee shakes a flower with its muscles.
senses.example: Buzz pollination shook pollen free from the tomato flower.

senses.definition: A small protective cover some young caddisflies make using silk and material from the stream or pond around them.
senses.example: The caddisfly case was made with tiny grains of sand.

senses.definition: Oxygen gas mixed into water in a form many water animals can use to breathe.
senses.example: The trout took dissolved oxygen from the water through its gills.

senses.definition: The firm flap along the side of the head that protects the gills of many fish.
senses.example: A dark mark showed on the edge of the bluegill’s gill cover.

senses.definition: Regular travel by fish between places where they feed, grow, or reproduce.
senses.example: The salmon’s migration took it from the sea to a river.
